takeaway: Inferior epigastric artery: supplies rectus abdominis and the medial anterolateral wall, anastomoses with the superior epigastric. Hernias medial to it are direct; lateral are indirect.

question.text: Which statement regarding the inferior epigastric artery is incorrect?

answer.text: An inguinal hernia medial to the inferior epigastric artery is described as an indirect hernia.

lines.text: The inferior epigastric artery climbs up behind the rectus abdominis.
It supplies the rectus muscle and the medial part of the anterolateral abdominal wall.
Above the umbilicus it anastomoses with the superior epigastric artery, so a laparoscopic port can injure it.
Now picture it as the fence post of a seesaw.
lines.say: Now picture it as the fence post of a seesaw. (laugh)

lines.text: Lateral to the artery is the indirect hernia.
Medial to the artery is the direct hernia.
So saying medial means indirect is the incorrect statement.
